tooltip.title: Pemphigus Vulgaris (PV)
tooltip.markdown: An autoimmune blistering disease characterized by flaccid bullae and painful erosions on skin and mucous membranes. It is potentially life-threatening if untreated.

tooltip.title: Pathophysiology of PV
tooltip.markdown: Understanding the molecular mechanisms of pemphigus vulgaris

tooltip.title: Acantholysis
tooltip.markdown: Antibodies disrupt desmosomal adhesion, causing keratinocytes to separate

tooltip.title: Blister Level
tooltip.markdown: Leads to a suprabasal intraepidermal split

tooltip.title: Clinical Features of PV
tooltip.markdown: Key clinical manifestations and physical findings

tooltip.title: Mucosal Erosions
tooltip.markdown: Painful oral erosions are the first sign in ~70% of patients

tooltip.title: Cutaneous Bullae
tooltip.markdown: Flaccid, fragile blisters on normal-appearing skin that rupture easily to form widespread, painful erosions

tooltip.title: Nikolsky Sign
tooltip.markdown: Positive. Gentle pressure on the skin causes the epidermis to shear off

tooltip.title: Histology
tooltip.markdown: Suprabasal acantholysis with a "row of tombstones" appearance

tooltip.title: Direct Immunofluorescence
tooltip.markdown: Intercellular "net-like" pattern of IgG and C3 deposition

tooltip.title: Serology
tooltip.markdown: Positive ELISA for anti-DSG3 and/or anti-DSG1 antibodies

tooltip.title: Adjuvant Therapy
tooltip.markdown: Steroid-sparing agents like Mycophenolate Mofetil or Azathioprine
